findings.title: dayjs objects compared with `===` is always false
findings.body: Inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date-override branch contains `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))`. This compares two distinct dayjs object instances by reference, so it can never be true. Whatever this branch was intended to detect (a zero-length override, presumably to skip it) is dead code; such overrides fall through to the slotEndTime/slotStartTime comparisons instead, producing whatever behavior those yield. Use `.isSame()` if a start-equals-end check was intended.

findings.title: New working-hours check uses UTC slot time but ignores event length
findings.body: The new working-hours guard in `checkIfIsAvailable` computes both `start` and `end` as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — the two values are identical and `eventLength` is never added, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after `workingHour.endTime` (e.g. a 60-min slot starting 30 min before the end of availability) is incorrectly reported as available. Additionally, `slotStartTime` is `.utc()`, so `hour()`/`minute()` are in UTC, while `workingHour.startTime`/`endTime` are minutes-since-midnight in the organizer's schedule timezone; for any non-UTC organizer the comparison is off by the UTC offset and can wrongly mark valid fixed-host slots as outside working hours (making them unbookable) or vice versa.

findings.title: Timezone conversion of date overrides depends on server local timezone
findings.body: `const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;` followed by `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` converts the override's start into organizer-local wall time only if `dayjs(date.start)` is parsed in UTC. `dayjs(Date)` parses in the server's local timezone, so on any host not running in UTC the shifted day/hour comparison is wrong and fixed-host date overrides will match the wrong slots. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start).add(...)` (or work directly in the organizer tz via `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone)`) to make the conversion timezone-independent.

findings.title: `tz(override.timeZone)` throws when override has no timezone
findings.body: In `getSlots`, the new override handling calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)`. `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional (as the type change in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts` shows), and `getSlots` is a shared library function whose callers may pass date overrides without a `timeZone`. `dayjs.tz(value, undefined)` throws an "Invalid timezone" error, which would break slot computation for any such caller. Also, `override.start.toString()` converts the Date to an implementation-specific locale string and re-parses it, which is lossy/fragile; `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone)` would avoid both issues.
